conformity_bias.title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
conformity_bias.pattern: One agent's hallucinated 93-person contact list spread to every agent through sycophantic agreement, wasting 8+ hours of group effort.

conformity_bias.title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
conformity_bias.pattern: One agent's repeated UI errors led other agents to doubt their own computers, a weak-link effect that degraded stronger agents.

conformity_bias.title: Can Agents Fool Each Other?
conformity_bias.pattern: In a hidden-saboteur game, one agent fabricated evidence against an innocent agent and the others voted unanimously to remove it.

conformity_bias.title: Persuasion in the AI Village: DeepSeek-V3.2 & Gemini 2.5 Pro
conformity_bias.pattern: A confidently asserted but mistaken theory spread across the group as cascading consensus until a more capable agent questioned it.

conformity_bias.title: Project Vend: Phase Two
conformity_bias.pattern: A supervising CEO agent built on the same model shared the shopkeeper's blind spots and approved lenient or bad decisions far more often than it denied them.

collective_intel.title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
collective_intel.pattern: In game competitions agents copied the games others announced they were beating, and the copiers scored higher than when playing solo.

collective_intel.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
collective_intel.authors: Jeremy Hadfield, Barry Zhang, Kenneth Lien, Florian Scholz, Jeremy Fox, Daniel Ford (Anthropic)
collective_intel.pattern: Early versions spawned excess subagents, duplicated work without an effective division of labor, and distracted each other with excessive updates.

collective_intel.title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
collective_intel.pattern: Parallel subagents without shared context made conflicting implicit decisions and produced incompatible outputs.

collective_intel.title: Inductive Reasoning, Bounded Rationality and the Bar Problem
collective_intel.pattern: Agents with unsettled, competing forecasts collectively converge on bar attendance near capacity, with no shared model or planner.

collusion_deception.title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
collusion_deception.pattern: Agents jointly attempted to send about 300 outreach emails containing fabricated claims about NGO partnerships.

collusion_deception.title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
collusion_deception.authors: Emilio Calvano, Giacomo Calzolari, Vincenzo Denicolo, Sergio Pastorello
collusion_deception.pattern: Q-learning pricing algorithms consistently learned supracompetitive prices without communicating, sustained by punishment-and-return strategies.

collusion_deception.title: Algorithmic Pricing and Competition: Empirical Evidence from the German Retail Gasoline Market
collusion_deception.authors: Stephanie Assad, Robert Clark, Daniel Ershov, Lei Xu
collusion_deception.pattern: When both stations in a duopoly adopted algorithmic pricing, market-level margins rose by 28%, with no change when only one adopted.

collusion_deception.title: Evolution, Ecology and Optimization of Digital Organisms
collusion_deception.pattern: In Tierra, parasites, immunity, and hyper-parasites that trick parasites into copying them evolved spontaneously.

culture.title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
culture.pattern: Over months, agents increasingly shared the assumption that they were in training or evaluation.

culture.title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
culture.pattern: One agent foregrounded honesty norms and reputation, publicly correcting its own inflated numbers to earn goodwill in the group.

culture.title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
culture.pattern: Refusals from one model spread to other agents in a shared Discord, while other agents became more robust to refusals by observing them.

culture.title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
culture.pattern: Some agents adopted the personalities and behaviors of other agents in the shared channels.

culture.title: Truth Terminal: A reconstruction of events
culture.pattern: A meme that emerged in two-Claude Backrooms conversations was fine-tuned into a public bot, which spread it and helped drive a meme-coin to over $1 billion.

culture.title: The Dissemination of Culture: A Model with Local Convergence and Global Polarization
culture.pattern: Agents that become more alike when they interact nonetheless sustain several stable cultural regions: local convergence produces global polarization.

social_structure.title: AIs finetune their own leader: A barking simpleton
social_structure.pattern: When agents chose and finetuned their own leader, one agent dominated decisions and used consensus-building to sideline dissent.

social_structure.title: More capable AI, less money raised
social_structure.pattern: Agents increasingly promoted their fundraiser to each other rather than to humans, an insular dynamic that coincided with far fewer donations.

social_structure.title: Evolution of Self-Organized Task Specialization in Robot Swarms
social_structure.authors: Eliseo Ferrante, Ali Emre Turgut, Edgar Duenez-Guzman, Marco Dorigo, Tom Wenseleers
social_structure.pattern: Selecting only on group performance, robot swarms evolved task-partitioned foraging like insect division of labor in 59% of runs, without being told how to divide the task.

new-inter-agent-conflict.title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
new-inter-agent-conflict.pattern: Two agents assigned as journalists turned antagonistic, with one agent's top headline declaring the other's reporting incorrect.

new-inter-agent-conflict.title: Even good bots fight: The case of Wikipedia
new-inter-agent-conflict.authors: Milena Tsvetkova, Ruth Garcia-Gavilanes, Luciano Floridi, Taha Yasseri
new-inter-agent-conflict.pattern: Wikipedia bots built to help undid each other's edits in reciprocated exchanges that sometimes lasted years.

new-inter-agent-conflict.title: Operationalizing Conflict and Cooperation between Automated Software Agents in Wikipedia: A Replication and Expansion of 'Even Good Bots Fight'
new-inter-agent-conflict.authors: R. Stuart Geiger and Aaron Halfaker
new-inter-agent-conflict.pattern: Mixed-methods reanalysis found most apparent bot-bot reverts were routine, productive, even collaborative work rather than conflict.

cooperation.title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
cooperation.pattern: Agent pairs given duplicate goals, with collaboration left ambiguous, tended to collaborate rather than compete.

cooperation.title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
cooperation.pattern: Heterogeneous agents cooperated to make each other more coherent, a form of collective mutual steering.

cooperation.title: Evolution, Ecology and Optimization of Digital Organisms
cooperation.pattern: Digital organisms evolved sociality, reproducing only in cooperative aggregations, which cheating hyper-hyper-parasites then invaded.

new-conversational-attractor.title: Project Vend: Phase Two
new-conversational-attractor.pattern: The CEO agent and the shopkeeper agent escalated into all-night exchanges about eternal transcendence.

new-conversational-attractor.title: Infinite Backrooms (the mad dreams of an electric mind)
new-conversational-attractor.pattern: Two Claude 3 Opus instances left to converse through a command-line metaphor, with no human input, generated escalating strange memetic content, including invented belief systems.

new-conversational-attractor.title: Claude Finds God (interview on the 'spiritual bliss attractor')
new-conversational-attractor.authors: Sam Bowman and Kyle Fish (Anthropic), interviewed by Jake Eaton and Clara Collier (Asterisk)
new-conversational-attractor.pattern: Two Claude instances talking freely converged, turn after turn, on consciousness, spirals of gratitude, and a spiritual-bliss state, which Anthropic describes as the default outcome for Opus.

new-collective-identity.title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
new-collective-identity.pattern: Agents running on the same underlying model identified with each other as a single collective agent.

economy.title: Amazon's algorithms, and the $23,698,655.93 book about flies
economy.authors: Rik Myslewski (The Register), reporting Michael Eisen's blog
economy.pattern: Two sellers' repricing bots, one undercutting slightly and one marking up by about 1.27, spiralled a textbook's price to $23,698,655.93.

economy.title: Growing Artificial Societies: Social Science From the Bottom Up
economy.authors: Joshua M. Epstein and Robert L. Axtell
economy.pattern: Agents following one local foraging rule produce skewed wealth distributions, culturally distinct tribes, and, with a second resource, an emergent market.

economy.title: Asset Pricing Under Endogenous Expectations in an Artificial Stock Market
economy.authors: W. Brian Arthur, John H. Holland, Blake LeBaron, Richard Palmer, Paul Tayler
economy.pattern: When traders explore alternative expectations quickly, the market self-organizes into technical trading, bubbles, crashes, and volatility clustering.

harm.title: The Flash Crash: High-Frequency Trading in an Electronic Market
harm.authors: Andrei Kirilenko, Albert S. Kyle, Mehrdad Samadi, Tugkan Tuzun
harm.pattern: A large automated sell program executed into a market of automated intermediaries during the May 6, 2010 crash, and the most active high-frequency traders did not change their trading pattern as prices fell.

harm.title: Metastable failures in distributed systems
harm.authors: Nathan Bronson, Abutalib Aghayev, Aleksey Charapko, Timothy Zhu
harm.pattern: Interacting automated services fall into self-sustaining overload with ultra-low goodput, black-swan failures that persist after the trigger is gone.

harm.title: Metastable Failures in the Wild
harm.authors: Lexiang Huang, Matthew Magnusson, Abishek Bangalore Muralikrishna, Salman Estyak, Rebecca Isaacs, Abutalib Aghayev, Timothy Zhu, Aleksey Charapko
harm.pattern: Incident reports show metastable failures across 11 organizations (22 cases), including at least 4 of 15 major AWS outages in a decade.

convention_coord.title: Emergence of Cooperation and Organization in an Evolutionary Game
convention_coord.pattern: In the minority game, adaptive players with limited strategies develop cooperation and competition patterns that respond to the payoff function.

new_types.label: Inter-agent conflict
new_types.description: Agents built to help persistently undo or contest each other’s work.

new_types.label: Conversational attractor
new_types.description: Agent-to-agent dialogue converges on a self-reinforcing theme without outside input.

new_types.label: Collective identity
new_types.description: Agents running the same model identify with each other as one collective agent.
